pattern.crimePattern: a writer paid by a foundation forges a letter of authority to reach a dead commander's diaries, kills his widow when caught taking one, and finds she took the wrong year
pattern.notes: Fictional widow, writer, family and foundation; Milimani, Nakuru is a setting only. Mwalimu reads the diary entry over the phone in-case: "Call from Lands House, 4th floor (Records), re: Mwenda complaint. Instructed: close it." It closes the same complaint as the NFA file in case 60. The Ukarimu Foundation is new here and is pinned to t_kivuli.

ob.text: A house help reports her employer, Mama Felistus Koech (74), widow of the late Supt. Wilson Koech, found dead in her sitting room in Milimani estate, Nakuru. A bookshelf has been disturbed.

facts.text: Mama Felistus Koech was found dead in her sitting room in Milimani, Nakuru, on Tuesday morning; a bookshelf had been disturbed.
One blow to the head. Two cups of tea on the tray, both full.
On the side table: one brass candlestick, and a clean ring in the dust where its pair stood.
Twenty-nine diaries and one gap, where the jacket labelled twelve years ago stood.
Felistus's notebook: she lent Esther Wairimu the diary for twelve years ago and put the next year's volume in its jacket "so the shelf looks right".
On Felistus's desk: Kadzo Mwamuye's letter of introduction on Inspector-General's letterhead, authorising access to retired officers' papers.
Felistus's phone: a 30-minute call with Jepchumba on Monday at 18:20.
Atieno: "The writer came twice last week with a police letter. Mama said, 'She asks about one year only.' Last night Mama sent me home at seven: the writer was coming."
Atieno: she dusts the diary shelf every Monday morning; this Monday it was full.
The matatu conductor: Atieno rode home to Kaptembwo at 19:05.
Atieno: Mama was quarrelling with Mr. Kariuki next door about his hedge; the grandson wanted to sell the diaries online.

Hospital roster: Dr. Jepchumba Koech was on duty in Eldoret from 18:00 Monday to 08:00 Tuesday.
His church group: Kariuki was at a meeting in the church hall 18:30–21:00.
Mwalimu: "I have it. I borrowed it two weeks ago. I've read the page every night since." She was at home near Nyeri, three hours away.
Mwalimu reads it aloud: "Call from Lands House, 4th floor (Records), re: Mwenda complaint (Bahati Block 9). Instructed: close it. Do not minute. Told Wairimu NFA. She objected."

Records: Kadzo's grant is paid by the Ukarimu Foundation.

interrogations.intro: Kadzo sets a notebook and two pens on the table. "I last visited Mrs. Koech on Saturday. My letter is genuine; Police Headquarters authorised my research."
Kibet keeps his headset on. "I never told anyone about Grandpa's diaries."
Dr. Jepchumba, by phone from a ward: "I hadn't spoken to Mother in a month. We fought about the house."
Kariuki takes off his cap. "We quarrelled about a hedge. I was at church."
Mama Atieno holds her apron in both hands and tells it straight.
Mwalimu answers on the first ring. "I have the diary, Amani."

reconstruction.text: After her confession in case 70, Mwalimu asks Felistus for her husband's diary for the year Joseph died. Felistus lends it, and slips the next year's volume into the old jacket so the shelf won't show a gap.

Kadzo, whose "history" is funded by the Ukarimu Foundation, is offered three million more to bring back that one diary. She buys the address from Kibet and comes twice with a forged letter. Felistus refuses her both times.

On Monday at 19:25 Kadzo comes a third time. When Felistus goes to make tea, Kadzo pulls the labelled jacket off the shelf. Felistus comes back and tries to take it; Kadzo strikes her with a brass candlestick.
She leaves at 19:55 with the diary and the candlestick. In her hotel room she opens it: the following year. At 07:10 she texts "Maina — Ukarimu": wrong year.

afterVerdict.beat: Mwalimu drives to Nairobi. In Halima's office she gives a sworn statement about the Mwenda complaint and the nine-day file, and hands over the diary.
Halima reads the entry twice. "'She objected.' You never told us that part, Esther." Mwalimu: "It didn't matter. I signed."
The Ukarimu Foundation is pinned to the Pattern File. Amani's notebook: "Records, 4th floor. Third time."
